```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Figures and tables come from npn_fire/scripts/90_nf_figs.R (figs/<figure>_<profile>.png +
# manifest.csv; tables/*.csv). Everything on this page is summarised to EPA Level II ecoregions.
figs <- if (file.exists("figs/manifest.csv")) {
  utils::read.csv("figs/manifest.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
} else data.frame(figure = character(), profile = character())

show_fig <- function(name, caption, alt = caption) {
  m <- figs[figs$figure == name, , drop = FALSE]
  pick <- intersect(c("full", "dev"), m$profile)
  pick <- pick[file.exists(sprintf("figs/%s_%s.png", name, pick))]
  if (!length(pick)) {
    cat(sprintf('\n::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n## Figure pending\n%s\n:::\n\n', caption))
    return(invisible())
  }
  r <- m[m$profile == pick[1], ][1, ]
  note <- sprintf("[%s &middot; %s &middot; figure made %s]{.fig-meta}", r$extent, r$years, r$made)
  cat(sprintf('\n![%s %s](figs/%s_%s.png){#fig-%s fig-alt="%s" .column-page-right}\n\n',
              caption, note, name, pick[1], gsub("_", "-", name), alt))
}
tab <- function(f) { p <- file.path("tables", f); if (file.exists(p)) utils::read.csv(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) else NULL }
fmt <- function(x, d = 0) format(round(x, d), big.mark = ",", nsmall = d, trim = TRUE)
RY <- tab("nf_record_years.csv"); GR <- tab("nf_groups.csv"); INV <- tab("nf_inventory_sites.csv")
n_rec <- if (!is.null(RY)) fmt(sum(RY$records) / 1e6, 1) else "29.4"
n_py <- if (!is.null(RY)) fmt(sum(RY$plant_years) / 1e6, 2) else "1.38"
n_ok <- if (!is.null(RY)) fmt(sum(RY$usable_onsets)) else "409,000"
yr_rng <- if (!is.null(RY)) paste0(min(RY$year), "&ndash;", max(RY$year)) else "2009&ndash;2024"
cls_lab <- c(initial_growth = "initial growth", young_leaves = "young leaves", leaves = "leaves", colored_leaves = "colored leaves",
             falling_leaves = "falling leaves", flowers = "flowers or buds", open_flowers = "open flowers", pollen = "pollen release",
             end_flowering = "end of flowering", fruits = "fruits", unripe_fruits = "unripe fruits", ripe_fruits = "ripe fruits",
             fruit_drop = "fruit or seed drop")
date_lab <- c(onset = "first", end = "last", up50 = "reaches 50 %", down50 = "below 50 % after peak")
ev_label <- function(ev) vapply(ev, function(e) { d <- sub("^.*_", "", e); c0 <- sub("_[^_]*$", "", e)
  paste0(if (is.na(cls_lab[c0])) c0 else cls_lab[[c0]], ": ", if (is.na(date_lab[d])) d else date_lab[[d]]) }, "")
glab <- c(deciduous_tree = "Deciduous trees", conifer = "Conifers", evergreen_tree = "Evergreen broadleaf trees",
          deciduous_shrub = "Deciduous shrubs", evergreen_shrub = "Evergreen shrubs", grass = "Grasses", forb = "Forbs")
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Work in progress
This page is updated as the analysis runs. Results are preliminary and will change. The study stands
on its own (its own data, units and code). Related pages: the [NPN grass curing study](npn_study.html),
the [fire activity study](fire_study.html) (satellite curing and fire in six pilot regions) and the
[fuel phenology regions](index.html).
:::

## At a glance

**The question.** Do the seasons that USA National Phenology Network (NPN) observers record on the
ground (leaf-out, flowering, leaf color and leaf fall, grass and forb green-up and drying) line up with
when fire seasons open and close? Where the record is deep enough, do early and late phenology years
shift fire activity? And, as a result in its own right: **where across the contiguous U.S. do NPN
observations and fire activity overlap** in place, season and year, so that NPN could inform wildfire
management, and where would more monitoring help?

**Why it matters.** Fire managers judge live fuels by eye and by fixed calendars; satellite and
weather indices stand in for plants that are rarely observed. NPN is the largest ground record of plant
seasons in the country, collected by volunteers, partner organizations and NEON. Its value for fire has
not been assessed across fuel types and regions. This study does that with the fire records already
assembled for the project.

**Approach, simplest first.**

1. **Where they align (inventory).** NPN sites and usable dates by EPA Level II ecoregion, plant group,
   phenophase and year; fire activity by ecoregion, fuel type, week and year. Where do both exist in the
   same seasons and years? This decides which tests below are possible anywhere.
2. **Seasonal alignment.** In each ecoregion, does the weekly fire curve in a fuel type change at the
   typical date of the matching phenophase (e.g. fewer fires in deciduous forest after leaf-out), beyond
   the seasonal cycle of dryness?
3. **Year to year, where the record allows.** In ecoregions with enough sites each year, does an early
   or late phenology year shift fire activity after a dryness baseline? Expected to be possible in only a
   few places; reported as feasibility and as the monitoring it would take.

**No satellite phenology** is used: this is a test of the ground record. Satellite fire detections
appear only as a fire outcome.

**Status (`r format(Sys.Date(), "%B %-d, %Y")`).** The NPN record is downloaded and cleaned
(`r n_rec` million status records, `r yr_rng`), plants are grouped, fire activity and the dryness baseline are tabulated by
ecoregion and fuel type, and the inventory (step 1) shows where the tests are possible. Next: the
seasonal test (step 2).

## Data and methods

### Data

- **NPN observations.** Every plant status and intensity record for the contiguous U.S., 2009–2024
  (the Nature's Notebook era), downloaded from the NPN data service. On each visit an observer records,
  for a tagged plant and each of its phenophases, whether the phase is present (yes / no) and, for many
  phases, how much (an intensity class: percent of the canopy full, percent of leaves colored, percent
  of a grass still green, or counts of buds, flowers and fruits). All plant groups are included,
  conifers too; animals are not. NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network) records are part of the
  same data set and are tracked separately.
- **Plant groups.** NPN's functional type gives grasses, forbs, conifers and cacti. Broadleaf woody
  species are split into trees and shrubs from USDA PLANTS growth habit; species PLANTS lists as both
  are split by mature height (20 ft and taller: tree). The 30 most-observed species still unresolved
  (cultivars, genus-only names, desert trees) were assigned by hand.
- **Fire.** Three records assembled for the [fire activity study](fire_study.html):
  **FPA-FOD** (7th edition), wildfire starts of all sizes 2001–2024 with debris and open burning removed;
  **MTBS** large-fire perimeters (wildfire and wildland fire use) 2001–2024 (2024 not yet complete);
  **VIIRS** 375 m active-fire detections 2012–2024 linked to reported wildfires, with cropland and
  unlinked detections removed.
- **Fuels.** LANDFIRE 2023 fire behavior fuel models (Scott and Burgan 40), grouped into grass,
  grass-shrub, shrub, timber-understory, timber litter and slash, as shares of each 4 km cell.
- **Units.** EPA / CEC Level II ecoregions (CEC 1997); Level III as a check where the record is dense.
- **Weather.** PRISM daily precipitation and temperature, for a 60-day water balance (precipitation
  minus Hargreaves potential evapotranspiration) as the dryness baseline, by ecoregion and fuel type.

### Methods

- **Dates.** For each tagged plant, phenophase and year: the **onset** is the first "yes" and the
  **end** the last "yes". An onset counts as *usable* when the previous visit, at most 14 days before,
  recorded "no" (7- and 30-day versions as checks); the same rule applies to ends. Phenophases are
  grouped across NPN protocols into NPN's 13 plant phenophase classes (initial growth, young leaves,
  leaves, colored leaves, falling leaves, flowers, open flowers, pollen, end of flowering, fruits,
  unripe fruits, ripe fruits, fruit drop).
- **Intensity dates.** Percent classes are converted to their midpoints (a "no" counts as 0 %). Two
  dates per plant-year: the first reading at or above 50 % (e.g. canopy half full) and the first
  reading below 50 % after the season's peak (e.g. a grass half cured). NPN intensity starts in 2011.
- **Cleaning.** Uncertain readings are dropped; repeat visits on one day are merged (yes if any
  observer said yes; highest intensity). Sites whose coordinates fall outside the contiguous U.S. or
  far from any ecoregion are left out of the ecoregion tables.
- **Year departures** (step 3) will be measured from each plant's own typical date and averaged to
  the ecoregion and year, weighting sites, not plants, so that changes in who observes don't read as
  changes in the plants.
- **Fire by fuel type.** Each fire is split over the LANDFIRE fuel-group shares of its 4 km cell (MTBS:
  of every burned cell, by burned area). Plant groups are matched to fuel groups in step 1 (deciduous
  and conifer trees with timber fuels, shrubs with shrub fuels, grasses and forbs with grass fuels).
  Weeks are fixed 7-day blocks from January 1, as in the fire activity study.
- **Which fire record leads** is set before any test is run: in each ecoregion and fuel type, the
  outcome with the best coverage in the inventory is reported first, the others as checks.

## The NPN record

The download holds `r n_rec` million plant status records from `r yr_rng`. Cleaned to one row per plant,
phenophase and year, that is `r n_py` million plant-years, of which `r n_ok` have a usable onset. The
record grew quickly after 2011 and has held at about 15,000 plants a year since 2017, while the number
of sites peaked in 2020–21 and has fallen since: fewer sites, observed more often.

```{r fig-record}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_record", "The NPN plant record by year: status records, plants observed (with the range of sites a year) and usable onsets.")
```

```{r fig-groups}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_groups", "Usable onsets by plant group, split by kind of phenophase. Deciduous trees dominate the record; grasses, the fuel the other studies centre on, are a small part.")
```

```{r tbl-groups}
#| tbl-cap: "Usable onsets by plant group and kind of phenophase, all years."
if (!is.null(GR)) {
  d <- GR[order(-GR$total), c("label", "Leaves", "Flowers", "Fruits", "total")]
  names(d) <- c("Plant group", "Leaves", "Flowers", "Fruits", "Total")
  for (k in 2:5) d[[k]] <- fmt(d[[k]])
  knitr::kable(d, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr")
}
```

## Where the record is

Sites with at least one usable leaf-out-type onset (initial growth, young leaves or leaves), by
ecoregion and plant group, over the whole record:

```{r fig-effort-map}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_effort_map", "Level II ecoregions shaded by the number of sites with a usable leaf-out-type onset, per plant group (numbers shown where 5 or more).")
```

Deciduous trees and shrubs are observed almost everywhere, and densely across the East. Conifers and
evergreen shrubs have a moderate record in the West and Northeast. Grasses are thin everywhere, with no
more than about 20 sites in any ecoregion over the whole record, the same limit the
[NPN grass curing study](npn_study.html) found.

Year-to-year tests need sites every year, not only over the whole record:

```{r fig-effort-years}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_effort_years", "Sites with a usable onset of any kind, by ecoregion and year. The NPN curing study found that about 10 sites give a reliable regional mean for a year.")
```

```{r tbl-inventory}
#| tbl-cap: "Sites with a usable leaf-out-type onset by ecoregion and plant group, whole record (ecoregions with 20 or more sites in a group)."
if (!is.null(INV)) {
  lab <- c(deciduous_tree = "Decid. tree", deciduous_shrub = "Decid. shrub", conifer = "Conifer", evergreen_shrub = "Evergr. shrub",
           grass = "Grass", forb = "Forb", evergreen_tree = "Evergr. tree", other = "Other")
  W <- stats::reshape(INV[, c("eco_l2_code", "eco_l2_name", "group", "sites")], idvar = c("eco_l2_code", "eco_l2_name"), timevar = "group", direction = "wide")
  names(W) <- sub("^sites\\.", "", names(W))
  cols <- intersect(names(lab), names(W)); W[cols][is.na(W[cols])] <- 0
  W <- W[apply(W[cols], 1, max) >= 20, ]
  o <- order(as.numeric(sub("\\..*", "", W$eco_l2_code)), as.numeric(sub("^\\d+\\.", "", W$eco_l2_code))); W <- W[o, ]
  nm <- gsub("\\bUsa\\b", "USA", tools::toTitleCase(tolower(W$eco_l2_name)))
  d <- data.frame(Ecoregion = paste(W$eco_l2_code, nm), W[cols], check.names = FALSE)
  names(d)[-1] <- lab[cols]
  knitr::kable(d, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

## Fire activity by fuel type

The three fire records, tabulated by ecoregion, week and fuel type: 1.48 million FPA-FOD wildfires of
all sizes 2001–2024 (after removing 459,000 debris and open burns; 193,000 of them 10 acres or larger),
10,400 MTBS wildfire perimeters, and 1.7 million VIIRS active-fire pixel-days 2012–2024 linked to
reported wildfires. Every fire falls in a Level II ecoregion.

```{r fig-fire}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_fire_fuel", "Fuel mix of the fire records by ecoregion: share of each record by LANDFIRE fuel group of the fire's 4 km cell, with the average number per year. FPA-FOD wildfires of all sizes (2001&ndash;2024) and VIIRS active-fire pixel-days linked to wildfires (2012&ndash;2024).")
```

What this shows for matching plant groups to fires:

- **Timber fuels carry most fires in the forested East and Northwest.** Timber litter and
  timber-understory cells hold 55–72 % of FPA-FOD wildfires in the Southeastern USA Plains, the
  Ozark / Ouachita–Appalachian Forests, the Atlantic Highlands, the Marine West Coast Forest and the
  Western Cordillera. These are also the ecoregions with the densest NPN record of deciduous trees, so
  leaf-out and leaf-fall can be set against these fires directly.
- **Grass and grass-shrub fuels carry most fires on the Plains and in the deserts:** 44–82 % of
  FPA-FOD wildfires in the semiarid prairies, the deserts, the Western Sierra Madre Piedmont and the
  Upper Gila Mountains. NPN's grass record is thin there (about 20 sites at most per ecoregion), though
  forbs and shrubs are observed more widely.
- **Many reported wildfires start in farmed or developed land.** A quarter of all FPA-FOD wildfires
  fall in cells that are mostly nonburnable (agriculture, urban, barren), and two-thirds in the
  Central USA Plains. These fires burn small patches of fuel that a 4 km fuel share can't place; step 1
  will report them separately rather than assign them to a plant group.
- **VIIRS adds little in the East.** After the fire study's screens (detections linked to a reported
  wildfire, cropland removed), eastern ecoregions keep 13 to 2,000 pixel-days a year, against 8,000–91,000
  in the larger western ones. Most eastern wildfires are small and short, and much eastern burning is
  prescribed or agricultural. FPA-FOD will likely be the lead record in the East; in the West all three
  records have enough fires to compare. The choice is made by the rule set out under Methods.

## Where NPN and fire line up (step 1)

```{r inv-setup}
#| include: false
TT <- tab("nf_inventory_tiers.csv"); T3 <- tab("nf_inventory_tier3.csv")
n_t2 <- if (!is.null(TT)) sum(TT$best_tier >= 2) else NA
n_t3 <- if (!is.null(TT)) sum(TT$best_tier == 3) else NA
n_eco <- if (!is.null(TT)) length(unique(TT$eco_l2_code)) else NA
```

Each plant group is matched to the fuels its fires burn in: trees and conifers to timber-understory
and timber-litter fuels; shrubs to shrub and grass-shrub fuels; grasses and forbs to grass and
grass-shrub fuels. Every phenophase NPN records is tested: for each of NPN's 13 plant phenophase classes
(initial growth, young leaves, leaves, colored leaves, falling leaves, flowers or buds, open flowers,
pollen release, end of flowering, fruits, unripe fruits, ripe fruits, fruit or seed drop), the first and
the last date it is seen; and for the five classes recorded as a percentage (young leaves, leaves,
colored leaves, open flowers, ripe fruits), the date it reaches 50 % and the date it drops below 50 % after
its peak (for grasses and forbs, the drop in leaves below 50 % green is curing). That makes 36 events. For
each, every ecoregion gets a typical date (the median of its sites' own typical dates) and a fire window of
four weeks either side of it. The rules below were fixed before any test was run:

- **Usable date:** bracketed by a "no" (or, for intensity dates, a reading on the other side of 50 %)
  within 14 days; a site's date for a year is the median over its plants.
- **Covered year:** a year with NPN dates in which a fire record has at least 10 fires (or pixel-days)
  in the matched fuel inside the window.
- **Lead fire record:** the one with the most covered years; ties go to FPA-FOD all sizes, then VIIRS,
  FPA-FOD 10 acres and up, MTBS.
- **Seasonal test possible:** 10 or more sites over the record and 5 or more covered years.
- **Year-to-year test possible:** 8 or more years that each have 10 or more sites and are covered.

```{r fig-inventory}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_inventory", "The furthest test the record supports, by ecoregion and plant group. Numbers: events (of 36) where the seasonal test is possible; where the year-to-year test is possible, events at that level / events at the seasonal level.")
```

Of the `r n_eco` ecoregions with NPN dates, the seasonal test is possible for at least one plant group and
event in `r n_t2` ecoregion × group combinations, and the year-to-year test in `r n_t3`. FPA-FOD wildfires of
all sizes lead almost everywhere: they are the only record with enough fires near most events, in the
East especially. The pattern follows the record: **deciduous trees** reach the year-to-year test across
the forested East, the Northwest, the Cold Deserts and California; **shrubs** in California, the deserts and
the Southeast; **forbs** in the eastern forests. **Grasses** reach the seasonal test in several ecoregions
but the year-to-year test in none, the same limit the NPN curing study found for its grass record.

```{r tbl-tier3}
#| tbl-cap: "Where the year-to-year test is possible: ecoregion, plant group and events."
if (!is.null(TT)) {
  d <- TT[TT$best_tier == 3, ]
  o <- order(as.numeric(sub("\\..*", "", d$eco_l2_code)), as.numeric(sub("^\\d+\\.", "", d$eco_l2_code)), d$group); d <- d[o, ]
  ev <- vapply(strsplit(d$tier3_events, ", "), function(x) paste(ev_label(x), collapse = "; "), "")
  nm <- gsub("\\bUsa\\b", "USA", tools::toTitleCase(tolower(d$eco_l2_name)))
  knitr::kable(data.frame(Ecoregion = paste(d$eco_l2_code, nm), `Plant group` = glab[d$group], Events = ev, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

## Do fire seasons change at the phenology dates? (step 2)

```{r seas-setup}
#| include: false
SS <- tab("nf_seasonal_summary.csv"); SRt <- tab("nf_seasonal_results.csv")
n_case <- if (!is.null(SRt)) nrow(SRt) else NA
n_dir <- if (!is.null(SRt)) sum(SRt$expected != "none") else NA
n_dirok <- if (!is.null(SRt)) sum(SRt$expected != "none" & ((SRt$expected == "down" & SRt$ratio < 1) | (SRt$expected == "up" & SRt$ratio > 1))) else NA
n_pass <- if (!is.null(SRt)) sum(SRt$pass %in% TRUE & SRt$expected != "none") else NA
```

For each case where the inventory allows it, the weekly fire rate in the matched fuel is compared before
and after the event's typical date, within eight weeks either side, with the year and the week's
dryness (the 60-day water balance where that fuel grows) held fixed. The **ratio** is the fire rate from
the typical date on, relative to before. Expected directions were set in advance (1 November 2026, before
any result of this test was seen):

| Phenophase class | First seen | Last seen | Reaches 50 % | Below 50 % after peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Initial growth | fewer fires | &ndash; | | |
| Young leaves | fewer | &ndash; | fewer | &ndash; |
| Leaves (incl. grass % green) | fewer | more | fewer | more |
| Colored leaves | more | &ndash; | more | &ndash; |
| Falling leaves | more | &ndash; | | |
| Flowers or buds | more | &ndash; | | |
| Open flowers | more | more | more | &ndash; |
| Pollen release | more | &ndash; | | |
| End of flowering | more | &ndash; | | |
| Fruits, unripe fruits | more | &ndash; | | |
| Ripe fruits | more | &ndash; | more | &ndash; |
| Fruit or seed drop | more | &ndash; | | |

Leaf-out stages are expected to bring fewer fires as live foliage replaces dry fuel; leaf color, leaf fall and
curing more. Flowering and the fruit stages are expected to bring more fires, following research reporting
that live fuel moisture falls after flowering. "&ndash;" marks events with no expected direction: their
results are reported and judged in either direction.

A ratio can differ from 1 just because the fire season is rising or falling at that time of year for
other reasons. So each ratio is also computed at every other week of the year (placebo dates, at least
five weeks from the real one); a case **passes** when its ratio lies beyond 90 % of the placebo ratios
in the expected direction (either direction where none is expected). With 36 events, seven plant groups and
up to 20 ecoregions, single cases are expected to pass by chance now and then; the evidence is in how
consistently an event passes across ecoregions and plant groups.

```{r fig-seas-curves}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_seasonal_curves", "Fire rate by week from each event's typical date: median over ecoregions of the weekly fire rate in the matched fuel, relative to the window's mean (FPA-FOD wildfires).")
```

```{r fig-seas-matrix}
#| results: asis
show_fig("nf_seasonal_matrix", "Seasonal test by phenophase event and plant group: ecoregions passing the placebo-date check out of those tested (FPA-FOD wildfires). Expected direction in brackets.")
```

Of `r n_case` cases, `r n_dir` have an expected direction; the ratio goes that way in `r n_dirok`, and
`r n_pass` also pass the placebo check.

```{r tbl-seas}
#| tbl-cap: "Seasonal test by plant group and event, where 5 or more ecoregions were tested (FPA-FOD wildfires): cases, median ratio, cases in the expected direction and cases passing the placebo check, with the ecoregions that pass."
if (!is.null(SS)) {
  SS <- SS[SS$cases >= 5, ]
  d <- data.frame(`Plant group` = glab[SS$group], Event = ev_label(SS$event), Expected = c(down = "fewer", up = "more", none = "&ndash;")[SS$expected],
                  Cases = SS$cases, `Median ratio` = SS$median_ratio, `Expected direction` = ifelse(SS$expected == "none", "&ndash;", SS$expected_direction),
                  Pass = SS$pass, `Passing ecoregions` = SS$pass_ecoregions, check.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(d, row.names = FALSE, escape = FALSE)
}
```

## Next steps

1. **Year to year (step 3)** where the inventory allows it: does an early or late event year shift fire in
   the window around it, beyond the dryness baseline?
2. Checks on step 2: the other fire records (FPA-FOD 10 acres and up, VIIRS, MTBS) where they have enough
   fires, and the 7- and 30-day date rules.

## Decisions

| Date | Decision |
|---|---|
| Oct 25 | A separate study of NPN's potential for wildfire applications across CONUS, without satellite phenology |
| Oct 31 | All NPN plant status and intensity records (conifers included, no animals); EPA Level II ecoregions; evaluate FPA-FOD, MTBS and VIIRS; self-contained code |
| Nov 1 | Broadleaf trees vs shrubs from USDA PLANTS growth habit, then mature height (20 ft); 30 species by hand |
| Nov 1 | LANDFIRE fuel groups as the fuel layer; FPA-FOD all sizes and 10 acres and up; VIIRS from the fire study's CONUS-wide screen |
| Nov 1 | Mesquites, paloverdes and Joshua tree counted as shrubs; shrubs matched to shrub and grass-shrub fuels; inventory rules fixed before testing |
| Nov 1 | Seasonal test design (step 2) approved and fixed before testing: negative binomial with year and dryness, eight weeks either side, placebo dates, expected directions set in advance |
| Nov 1 | All 13 NPN plant phenophase classes tested (36 events); flowering and fruit stages expected to bring more fires (fuel moisture drops after flowering); set before any step 2 result was seen |
